metadata.title: Perceo — local-first dev suite for agent operators
metadata.description: Three self-hosted tools for people who run coding and computer-use agents all day. Dispatch agents across isolated workspaces, run them on real desktops, and keep what they learn.

footer.headline: Runs on your machine. Ends at your machine.
footer.description: Your repos, your VMs, your notes, your keys. No account, no control plane, no telemetry endpoint.

metadata.title: Products | Perceo
metadata.description: Archductor, Archfleet, and Archivum — three self-hosted tools for running agents on your own hardware.

productsPage.title: Three tools, one stack.
productsPage.description: Everything here is self-hosted and runs on your own machine. Dispatch coding agents across isolated workspaces, run computer-use agents on real desktops, and keep what they learn. Each tool works on its own; none of them require the others.

products.name: Archductor
products.summary: Desktop control plane for running coding agents across isolated Git worktree workspaces.
products.pitch: One workspace per task: Git worktree, branch, Codex or Claude Code session, diff review, PR merge. Use it when one codebase has several streams of work in flight and you do not want branch state, terminal state, or half-finished diffs bleeding together.

detail.tagline: Desktop control plane for coding agents.
detail.intro: Create a workspace, start Codex or Claude Code, review the diff, open or merge a GitHub pull request, archive the workspace, then start the next task without leaving the app.
detail.note: Linux is the primary validated target. Windows is a preview target. Inspired by Conductor.
points: Give each workspace its own Git worktree, branch, .context directory, and stable ARCHDUCTOR_PORT range.
Run multiple workspaces for the same repository in parallel without them trampling each other.
Start multiple Shell, Codex, or Claude Code sessions inside one workspace.
Review changed files, diffs, todos, comments, PR checks, and sibling workspace conflicts in one surface.
Create, refresh, merge, and archive GitHub PRs through your own local gh auth.
workflow: Add an existing repository or clone a Git URL.
Configure scripts, prompts, and workspace defaults in .archductor/settings.toml.
Create a workspace from a branch, prompt, GitHub issue, GitHub PR, or Linear issue.
Start Codex, Claude Code, or shell sessions inside it.
Review the diff, checks, todos, comments, and conflicts.
Create or merge the PR, archive the workspace, then repeat.

installTargets.name: Homebrew / Linuxbrew
installTargets.command:
brew tap perceo-ai/tap
brew install archductor

installTargets.name: AppImage
installTargets.command:
curl -Lo archductor.AppImage \
  https://github.com/perceo-ai/conductor-arch/releases/latest/download/archductor-x86_64.AppImage
chmod +x archductor.AppImage
sudo mv archductor.AppImage /usr/local/bin/archductor

requirements: Linux desktop with GTK4/libadwaita support, or the Windows preview build.
git for worktrees, branches, diffs, and commits.
gh authenticated with gh auth login for PRs, checks, comments, and merges.
Your existing local codex or claude authentication, if you want agent sessions.

products.name: Archfleet
products.summary: Fleet manager for computer-use agents running on isolated VMs.
products.pitch: Draw a workflow, run it on an isolated libvirt VM driven by Agent S, and take over via XRDP when it gets stuck. Computer-use agents need a real desktop; this gives each run its own instead of yours.

detail.intro: Computer-use agents need a real desktop — a window manager, a browser with a profile, a file picker, a login session. Giving one your actual machine is not something you want to do twice. Archfleet gives each run its own VM instead.
detail.note: Archfleet is the newest product in the suite and is in active development. Install and configuration docs land with the first tagged release.
points: Define what the agent should accomplish as a workflow, not a single prompt.
Each run gets its own libvirt guest, so nothing the agent does touches the host.
Agent S drives the desktop inside the guest; Archfleet owns VM lifecycle, scheduling, and run history.
Connect over XRDP and drive the session yourself when the agent stalls.
workflow: Draw the workflow the agent should follow.
Archfleet provisions an isolated libvirt guest for the run.
Agent S perceives and acts inside the guest desktop.
Watch the run, or take over via XRDP when it gets stuck.
Keep the trace as evidence of what the product actually did.
requirements: A libvirt/KVM host with capacity for the guests you want to run in parallel.
Guest images with a desktop environment and XRDP.

products.name: Archivum
products.summary: Self-hosted second brain with a built-in MCP server.
products.pitch: The wiki that writes itself. Drop in a PDF or paste a URL and Archivum writes the page, links related concepts, and keeps it searchable — then serves the whole thing to your agents through a built-in MCP server.

detail.intro: Repos carry code. They do not carry the reasoning: why a decision went the way it did, which approach already failed, what a customer actually asked for. Archivum is where that lives, and MCP is what makes it reachable.
detail.note: One command to start. No cloud account, no SaaS, and no data leaving your machine unless you point it at a hosted model.
points: Ingest files and URLs; an LLM extracts structured notes and writes the wiki page.
A background agent maintains pages, vector embeddings, and the knowledge graph.
Semantic search and question answering over everything you have ingested.
A built-in MCP server so Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, or VS Code read the same notes you do.
Point OLLAMA_BASE_URL at a local model and nothing leaves the machine at all.
workflow: Run the bootstrap script, or clone the repo and copy .env.example.
Fill in your model key, JWT secret, owner password, and MCP key.
docker compose up -d, then open http://localhost.
Drop in documents and URLs; the background agent does the filing.
Point your MCP client at the server so agents read and write the same wiki.

installTargets.name: Manual (Docker Compose)
installTargets.command:
git clone https://github.com/pranavkannepalli/archivum.git
cd archivum
cp .env.example .env
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.images.yml up -d --no-build

requirements: Docker and Docker Compose on the host.
Node.js, for the guided installer CLI.
A model provider key, or a local Ollama endpoint.
